ai_insights.executive_summary: The test executed 765 samples across 18 journey iterations with 20 concurrent users over 235 seconds, achieving 3.25 req/s throughput and 31.76% transaction error rate. Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% (22 of 48 main transactions met targets), with widespread 100% error rates in critical paths and P90 latency breaching SLA targets by up to +165.6%. Server-side telemetry was unavailable, but time-series data shows latency remained stable under load while errors concentrated in specific transactions, indicating application-level failure rather than infrastructure saturation.

findings.title: Universal Application Errors in Critical User Journeys
findings.observation: Multiple transactions across all user stories exhibited 100% error rates: TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage (18/18), TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal (18/18), TC02_T_02_Select_Reptiles_Section (18/18), TC04_T_02_Navigate_To_Signon_Page (18/18), TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials (17/17), TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart (17/17), TC04_T_05_Update_Account_Preferences (17/17), TC02_T_08_Add_Parrot_To_Cart (15/15/15), TC02_T_09_Update_Cart_Quantities (15/15), TC04_T_06_View_Past_Order_History (16/16), TC04_T_07_View_Specific_Order_Details (16/16), TC03_T_09_Search_Keyword_Amazon (15/15), TC02_T_10_Apply_Coupon_Code (15/15), TC02_T_11_Remove_Item_From_Cart (14/14), TC02_T_12_Proceed_To_Checkout_Screen (14/14), all violating the 1.00% error rate SLA target.
findings.likely_cause: Systemic application failure preventing successful execution of core user flows, likely due to misconfigured endpoints, broken authentication, or missing backend services.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot complete essential tasks such as browsing, searching, adding to cart, or signing in, resulting in zero successful end-to-end journeys and direct revenue impact.
findings.recommendation: Immediately investigate application logs for 404 and 500 errors, validate endpoint availability and authentication mechanisms, and restore service integrity for core user journeys.
findings.validation: Re-run test after fix and verify 0% error rate in previously failing transactions with error rate below 1.00% SLA target.

findings.title: Widespread P90 Latency SLA Breaches in Page Load Transactions
findings.observation: TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage P90 latency reached 664.0ms against a 250ms SLA target (+165.6% deviation). TC02_T_01_Launch_Shopping_Catalog P90 was 665.0ms vs 250ms target (+166.0% deviation). TC04_T_11_Perform_User_Sign_Out P90 was 656.0ms vs 400ms target (+64.0% deviation). TC01_T_04_Select_Dogs_Category and TC01_T_03_Select_Dogs_Section both exceeded their 300ms SLA targets with P90 of 468.0ms and 469.0ms respectively (+56.0% and +56.3% deviation).
findings.likely_cause: Inefficient frontend rendering, unoptimized asset delivery, or missing caching for static content causing delayed page load times.
findings.why_it_matters: Slow page load times degrade user experience, increase bounce rates, and negatively impact conversion, especially on homepage and category navigation paths.
findings.recommendation: Optimize frontend performance by leveraging browser caching, compressing and minifying assets, using CDN for static resources, and reducing DOM complexity on high-traffic pages.
findings.validation: Re-test and confirm P90 latency for TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC02_T_01_Launch_Shopping_Catalog falls below 250ms SLA target.

findings.title: Stable Latency Under Load Indicates No Infrastructure Bottleneck
findings.observation: Time-series data shows average response time remained flat between 157-187 ms from 1m to 3m50s despite constant 20-user concurrency and throughput stabilizing at ~18.5 req/s. P95 latency stayed consistently between 375-378 ms during the same period, with only a brief drop to 105 ms avg RT at 4m when throughput fell to 7.9 req/s. No correlation between rising concurrency and increasing latency was observed.
findings.likely_cause: Application failures (errors) reduced effective load on the server, preventing infrastructure saturation and masking potential performance limits.
findings.why_it_matters: The observed latency stability is artificial due to high error rates; fixing errors will increase actual load and may reveal true infrastructure limits.
findings.recommendation: After resolving application errors, re-run the test to measure true system capacity and identify actual saturation point under full successful load.
findings.validation: Post-fix test should show increasing response times with sustained concurrency if infrastructure is nearing limits, or stable performance if headroom remains.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: Not reached due to application errors suppressing actual load; infrastructure showed no signs of saturation at 20 users with stable latency.
capacity_planning.analysis: Latency and throughput remained stable from 1m to 3m50s at 20 users, indicating no infrastructure saturation occurred. However, since over 30% of transactions failed, the true load on the system was significantly lower than intended. The observed stability is likely due to failed requests not reaching backend processing. Capacity planning cannot be reliably determined until application errors are resolved and full load is applied.

root_cause_assessment.finding: Universal application errors preventing successful transaction execution
root_cause_assessment.evidence: 14 transactions across 4 user stories showed 100% error rates (e.g., TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage: 18/18 errors, TC02_T_02_Select_Reptiles_Section: 18/18 errors), with error types including 404 and 500 as seen in error breakdown.
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Broken or misconfigured application endpoints, failed service dependencies, or authentication system failure blocking core user journeys.
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Review application and web server logs for 404 and 500 errors, validate endpoint routing, check dependency health (e.g., databases, APIs), and verify authentication service availability.

recommendations.title: Fix Core User Journey Endpoints
recommendations.why: Multiple critical transactions (homepage launch, search portal, login, cart operations) are failing at 100% rate, making the application unusable for core functions.
action: Audit and restore broken endpoints returning 404 errors
Investigate and resolve 500 Internal Server Errors in application logic
Validate authentication and session management flows
recommendations.expected_impact: Restore end-to-end journey success, enabling valid performance testing and real user functionality.
recommendations.validation: Re-run test and verify error rate drops below 1.00% SLA target for all previously failing transactions.

recommendations.title: Optimize Page Load Performance
recommendations.why: Homepage and category page loads exceed SLA targets by up to +166%, degrading user experience and increasing bounce risk.
action: Enable browser caching and CDN delivery for static assets
Compress and minify JavaScript, CSS, and HTML
Reduce DOM size and defer non-critical JavaScript
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduce P90 latency for TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC02_T_01_Launch_Shopping_Catalog below 250ms SLA target.
recommendations.validation: Re-test and confirm P90 latency for homepage and catalog launch transactions meets defined SLA targets.

executive_summary.assessment_text: The application suffered from universal critical errors in core user journeys, rendering it unusable for meaningful performance evaluation. Despite 20-concurrency load, latency remained stable due to failed requests not reaching backend processing. Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% with 26 of 48 transactions violating targets, primarily due to 100% error rates in key paths and P90 latency breaches in page load transactions.
assessment_bullets: Overall SLA compliance was 45.8% (22 of 48 main transactions met targets) with 31.76% transaction error rate over 765 samples
Multiple critical transactions exhibited 100% error rates (e.g., TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal), violating the 1.00% error SLA
TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage P90 latency reached 664.0ms vs 250ms target (+165.6% deviation), indicating severe page load performance issues
conclusions: Application is currently unusable for end-user transactions due to widespread endpoint failures
Observed latency stability is artificial; fixing errors will increase real load and may expose infrastructure limits
Immediate focus must be on restoring basic functionality before performance optimization can be meaningful
